cards.explanation: The answer is the cave at Makkedah. The five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah (Joshua 10:16). Five grown kings in one cave. I bet the last one in got the spot by the draft and had plenty to say about it.

The answer is to roll large stones against its mouth. Joshua says, "Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and post men there to guard them." The kings are found, and the cave becomes a shut door. Nobody walks out of there until Joshua says so.

The answer is to chase the enemy and attack from behind. Joshua tells his men, "But you, do not stop there. Pursue your enemies and attack them from behind." The kings are shut in the cave, so the rest of the men keep moving. No standing around by the stones for this crew.

The word is cities. Joshua says, "Do not let them reach their cities, for the LORD your God has delivered them into your hand." The text then says the survivors retreated to the fortified cities (Joshua 10:20). So the cities are where the enemy was headed.

The answer is False. The text says, "The whole army returned safely to Joshua in the camp at Makkedah…" No lost men are mentioned. I'd say that's good news for the camp, friends, and a lot of people probably counted heads twice.

The answer is True. The army comes back safe to Joshua at Makkedah, and the text says, "…no one dared to utter a word against the Israelites." Not one word. I bet that camp was quieter than a group chat after somebody types "we need to talk."

The answer is commanders. Joshua summons all the men of Israel, then speaks to the army commanders who had come with him. They come forward and put their feet on the necks of the kings (Joshua 10:24). Then Joshua tells them, "Be strong and courageous…"

The answer is that the LORD will do this to all their enemies. Joshua says, "Do not be afraid or discouraged… Be strong and courageous, for the LORD will do this to all the enemies you fight." His reason is the LORD, and nothing else. The courage comes from who is fighting with them.

The answer is False. The text says Joshua left the bodies on the trees "until evening." Then "At sunset Joshua ordered that they be taken down from the trees…" This is a heavy part, friends, so I'll just say it plainly and move on.

The answer is that the stones were still there when this was written. The text says the stones are there "…to this day." The writer tells us the stones were still at the mouth of that cave when it was written. At sunset the bodies were thrown into the cave, and then large stones were placed against its mouth.

The answer is the LORD, the God of Israel. The text says Joshua did this "…just as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded." This is a heavy part of the story, friends, and I think it's okay to feel that. The text tells us who gave the command: the LORD, the God of Israel.
The answer is False. Joshua 10:42 says he "…captured all these kings and their land in one campaign." That's a lot of cities in one trip. I can barely finish one batch before the timer goes off.

The answer is that the LORD fought for Israel. The text says, "…because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel, Joshua captured all these kings and their land in one campaign." The reason is the LORD. That matches what Joshua told his commanders earlier about being strong and courageous.

The answer is True! Verse 42 says Joshua captured all these kings and their land "…in one campaign." Then verse 43 says he "…returned with all Israel to the camp at Gilgal." One campaign, then straight home to camp. That's the person who finishes the whole errand list in one trip, and the rest of us come home missing the ONE thing.
